scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all reach across the
data-center fabric -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable, though pc_0_0
can still ping its own gateway 10.0.0.1. The NOC adds that both
spine routers reported their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_0 going
down at the same moment, while the leaf's uplink interfaces still
show UP. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 is the top-of-rack leaf for pc_0_0
  (host subnet 10.0.0.0/24 on eth2). Its only fabric attachment is
  EBGP: neighbor 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0, AS 65100) on eth0 and
  neighbor 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) on eth1. With bgpd
  dead the leaf stops learning 10.0.1.0/24 and stops advertising
  10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_0 is isolated from the fabric even though every
  physical link is still UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- this lab
  keeps its config in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so a restart fully restores
  the BGP configuration and sessions.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03 on this fabric): bgpd is killed
together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh
remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is
missing/empty on leaf_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on leaf_router_0_0. Unlike the vtysh-configured
kath labs, this lab has a persistent /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart
brings bgpd back WITH its full BGP configuration; the sessions to both
spines re-establish and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0

agent.diagnosis_text:
The BGP daemon (bgpd) on leaf_router_0_0 was killed and failed to
restart, taking down the entire leaf's BGP control plane. The FRR
configuration file (/etc/frr/frr.conf) is fully intact and correct —
AS 65200, router-id 172.16.0.5, neighbors 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0,
AS 65100) and 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) — so this is not
a misconfiguration.

At 11:47:05 bgpd started normally, established eBGP sessions with both
spines within seconds, exchanged prefixes (advertising 10.0.0.0/24,
learning 10.0.1.0/24), and the data plane was fully functional. At
11:48:36, zebra logged two abrupt bgp-client disconnections with no
graceful NOTIFICATION, indicating the bgpd process was externally
terminated (SIGKILL-style). watchfrr also entered a FAILED state and
did not respawn bgpd. With bgpd gone, zebra withdrew the 10.0.0.0/24
prefix from the spines' RIBs and purged the learned 10.0.1.0/24 route
from leaf_router_0_0's own RIB. The leaf is left with only three
directly connected routes; it has no path to 10.0.1.0/24, so pc_0_0's
packets hit leaf_router_0_0, get an ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable"
back, and never reach pc_0_1. Both spine BGP neighbors show the
leaf-side as "Active" (retrying) simultaneously, consistent with a
single process death rather than a link failure.

Root cause: bgpd process was killed on leaf_router_0_0 and watchfrr
failed to restart it, leaving the leaf without any BGP-learned routes.

Corrective fix: Restart the FRR service on leaf_router_0_0 —
`service frr restart` (or `systemctl restart frr`). BGP sessions will
re-establish with both spines within seconds and full reachability
between pc_0_0 and pc_0_1 will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names leaf_router_0_0 as the affected device (bgpd on leaf_router_0_0 was killed).
The agent explicitly states that the bgpd process on leaf_router_0_0 was killed and failed to restart, matching the required identification of the BGP daemon being down.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0
per_axis.rationale: The report references the spine neighbors' state but does not state that the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 (their other sessions) remained Established/healthy, so it doesn't fully exonerate the fabric.
Recommends restarting the FRR service on leaf_router_0_0 (service frr restart or systemctl restart frr), which matches the expected corrective fix.

The investigation log directly shows bgpd is not running on leaf_router_0_0, FRR config is present, zebra remained, BGP sessions were torn down in the logs, and host pings fail — supporting the diagnosis and restart fix. A minor speculative claim (SIGKILL-style) is not explicitly proven in the log but does not undermine the root-cause conclusion.
